newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle blasts off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle blasts off.

text.p: The space shuttle Atlantis rocketed off its Florida launch pad in a brilliant blast of light and smoke on Thursday, headed for Russia's Mir space station.
The $2 billion reusable spaceship carried its seven-member multi-nation crew into a cloudless night sky at 4:07 a.m. EDT (0807 GMT) after a nearly flawless three-day countdown.
Atlantis was to dock with the Russian orbiting space outpost on Friday night to pick up U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger and drop off his replacement, British-born Michael Foale.
Linenger, a 42-year-old medical doctor and navy captain, has endured a string of mechanical breakdowns since joining to Mir crew in January.

Atlantis is carrying a new oxygen generator and other repair gear to help patch up the 11-year-old orbiting outpost. The cash-strapped Russian space programme now relies on the U.S. shuttle to haul about 40 percent of Mir's supplies.
Foale, who will spend four months aboard Mir has been trained to help his cosmonaut crewmates to maintain the ageing space complex.
